newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraq says no U.S. air strikes from Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says no U.S. air strikes from Turkey.

text.p: An adviser to Iraqi President Saddam Hussein said on Thursday that Turkey had assured him it would not let U.S. planes strike Iraq from a base in southern Turkey.

"Turkey confirmed to us that the conditions by which the United States planes use Incirlik air base do not permit the United States to launch air strikes into Iraq," presidential envoy Hamed Youssef Hummadi told reporters.
He was speaking after two days of talks with senior Turkish officials.
U.S. jets were moving into position for possible bombing raids against Iraq after Baghdad forces fired a surface-to-air missile at U.S. fighters over northern Iraq on Wednesday.
Eight U.S. F-117A jets have flown to Kuwait and four B-52s moved to a British air base on the Indian Ocean island of Diego Garcia to be in closer striking range to Iraq.
But Turkey said it had received no request from NATO ally the United States for the use of the joint Turkish-U.S. air base at Incirlik, near the southern city of Adana.
"There has been no request," a foreign ministry official said. "They obviously don't need it at the present," he told Reuters.
The Iraqi SAM-6 missile fired on Wednesday missed the U.S. planes which were from a Western allied air force that enforces a no-fly zone over northern Iraq out of Incirlik.
